title: Single Molecule Imaging and Tracking of Processive Myosin Motors
author: Gardini, Arbore, et al.
materials: Materials:•Pure Ethanol•Nitrocellulose 1%: 10 mg nitrocellulose 0.45 μm pore size (Sigma N8267) dissolved in 1 ml pentyl acetate solution. (Tip: nitrocellulose 1% can be stored at 4 °C for few months)•Double sticky tape (˜ 60 μm thick)•Glass coverslips: 24 x 24 mm and 60 x 24 mm, ˜ 150 μm thick. Glass slides: 26 x 76 mm, ˜ 1 mm thick (purchased from VWR).

steps.title: Clean glass coverslip
steps.instruction: Take a 24 × 24 mm glass coverslip, wipe it with paper soaked in pure ethanol, rinse directly with pure ethanol using clean tweezers, then dry under a gentle nitrogen flow; repeat the whole cleaning once more if any residue remains.

steps.title: Apply nitrocellulose coating
steps.instruction: Place a second clean 24 × 60 mm coverslip on the cleaned coverslip and smear exactly 2 µl of 1 % nitrocellulose solution (10 mg nitrocellulose 0.45 µm pore size dissolved in 1 ml pentyl acetate) onto one surface; let it dry completely before proceeding.

steps.title: Clean microscope slide
steps.instruction: Take a 26 × 76 mm glass slide, wipe it with paper soaked in pure ethanol, and dry it under a nitrogen flow to remove coarse residues.

steps.title: Assemble flow chamber with tape
steps.instruction: Cut two narrow (~3 mm long) strips of double‑sticky tape (~60 µm thick) and affix them on one side of the slide to create a chamber of approximately 20 µl volume; chamber volume can be adjusted by changing tape spacing or thickness.

steps.title: Seal chamber with nitrocellulose side inward
steps.instruction: Using clean tweezers, place the nitrocellulose‑coated coverslip (from step 2) onto the taped slide so that the nitrocellulose‑coated surface faces the interior of the chamber, completing the flow cell.

steps.title: Prepare and chill all buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare the following buffers and keep them on ice: MB‑KCl (20 mM MOPS pH 7.4, 1 mM MgCl₂, 0.1 mM EGTA, 50 mM KCl, 1 mM DTT), MBα (MB‑KCl + 0.1 mg/ml α‑casein), Imaging Buffer (IB: MB‑KCl + 1.2 µM glucose oxidase, 0.2 µM catalase, 4.2 µM α‑casein, 17 mM glucose, 20 mM DTT), IB‑C (IB + 2 µM calmodulin), Reaction Mix (RM: IB + 0.1 mg/ml creatine phosphokinase, 5 mM creatine phosphate, 2 µM calmodulin, ATP at desired concentration), and 2× High‑Salt (HIS) buffer (1 M KCl, 40 mM KPi, 2 mM EGTA, 4 mM MgCl₂). Filter‑sterilize where indicated and store at 4 °C (IB must be freshly prepared every ~5 h).

steps.title: Introduce NEM‑myosin II and incubate
steps.instruction: Flux NEM‑myosin II (20 mg/ml) diluted to 2 mg/ml in 2× HIS buffer into the flow chamber and incubate exactly 1 minute on ice.

steps.title: Wash chamber with α‑casein buffer
steps.instruction: Flush the chamber with three chamber volumes of MBα buffer to remove unbound myosin.

steps.title: Add rhodamine‑phalloidin actin and incubate
steps.instruction: Flux 23 nM rhodamine‑phalloidin‑labeled F‑actin prepared in MB‑KCl containing 10 mM DTT into the chamber and wait 2 minutes on ice.

steps.title: Wash with imaging buffer
steps.instruction: Flush the chamber with four chamber volumes of Imaging Buffer (IB) to remove excess actin.

steps.title: Dilute QD‑HMM‑5B to 2 nM in IB‑C
steps.instruction: Mix 5 µl of the 40 nM QD‑HMM‑5B stock with 95 µl of IB‑C, yielding a 2 nM QD‑HMM‑5B solution; this dilution remains usable for 4–5 hours before a new conjugation is required.

steps.title: Optional test low‑density QD attachment
steps.instruction: Further dilute the 2 nM QD‑HMM‑5B solution to 0.1 nM in IB‑C, flux it into the chamber, and inspect under the microscope to confirm a reasonable number of QDs are bound to actin filaments.

steps.title: Dilute QD‑HMM‑5B in reaction mix with ATP
steps.instruction: Dilute the 2 nM QD‑HMM‑5B stock to 0.1 nM in Reaction Mix (RM) containing the desired ATP concentration, then flux this mixture into the chamber.

steps.title: Optional seal chamber with silicone grease
steps.instruction: Close the flow chamber carefully using silicone grease; alternatively keep the chamber open to allow exchange of QD‑HMM‑5B or ATP solutions on the same sample.

steps.title: Observe myosin movement under microscope
steps.instruction: Place the flow chamber on an inverted microscope and record movies of QD‑labeled myosin‑5B moving along the rhodamine‑actin filaments.

steps.title: Track gliding filaments and compute velocities
steps.instruction: Using ImageJ’s ‘Multitracker’ plugin, track filaments that travel >1 µm frame‑by‑frame; calculate instantaneous velocities, then compute each filament’s average velocity with standard error; obtain the final average velocity by weighted averaging across filaments (example: 163 ± 3 nm/s at 1 mM ATP, N = 20).

steps.title: Localize single QDs and extract trajectories
steps.instruction: Process single‑molecule movies with the PROOF software to localize each QD with ~4 nm precision (100 ms integration, 300 EM gain, 3 mW laser); derive myosin trajectories from x,y coordinates of QDs that persist ≥10 frames; analyze step size, run length, and velocity as a function of ATP concentration.
